tag: Episode 1 · I Became a Flower Pig
title: I Became a Flower Pig

beats.t: At some point, the fall softened and light wrapped around Yeoni. Their arms shrank, their fingers grew blunt. When they opened their eyes, they were in the middle of an enormous lotus-leaf boat floating on a river.
I TURNED INTO A PIIIIIG!
The scream carried across the night-dark river, then cut off. This body did not even have enough lung capacity left to keep screaming.

The lotus leaf was impossibly large, wider than a bed in most studio apartments, with dewdrops gleaming like lamps along its edge. No oars, no sail, no engine. Just a giant leaf. Yet it floated. Steadily, at that.
Yeoni stared down at themself for a long time. Short forelegs. A round belly. A curly tail. A little flower blooming on their head. However they looked at it, this pink body was not human.
No. ...How am I supposed to do my assignments with these hands?
An odd sound slipped into the end of their next sentence.
This makes absolutely no sense, oink.
Yeoni froze.
...What was that?
Hello. I am a human being.
That came out normally. Yeoni felt the tiniest bit relieved.
Okay. I can talk. At least there's that.
But then they looked at their forelegs again.
...My fingers are gone.
This is clearly a downgrade. From a human with ten fingers to a pig with two front hooves.
A moment ago, Yeoni had been in their room. Wet socks, a strange app, a tarot doorway. Now they were a pig with a flower. A flower pig, to be exact.
Yeoni flopped onto the lotus leaf. Their soft body squished a little, then sprang back. The sensation was so vivid that it only made things worse.
Okay. Got it. ...This is a dream.
Obviously. However weird the world had become, turning into a flower pig because you tapped the wrong app was going too far.
Yeoni tapped the leaf with a front hoof. They could feel it.
If it's a dream, I should pinch myself awake. ...My hoof can't reach my face.
...Nice graphics, though.
Yeoni reached a very serious conclusion. Having stayed up until three grinding a limited-time event, they were clearly suffering gaming aftereffects.
Status window.
Nothing appeared.
Menu. ...Inventory.
Only the wind passed. Yeoni narrowed their eyes.
...Terrible UI. One star.
Then a low voice came from the edge of the leaf.
Still feels like a dream? Can't blame you.
Yeoni went rigid. Slowly, they turned their head. Something was sitting at the leaf's edge.
At first they thought it was just a white cat. Small, round, fluffy. But on its head sat a navy wizard's hat with a golden crescent moon. A cat. Wearing a hat.
...What are you?
I am Yeongnyangi.
A cat?
No.
Then what? You look exactly like a cat in a hat.
To be precise, I am not an ordinary cat.
Then why are you so tiny? You'd fit in my palm.
Yeongnyangi's whiskers twitched.
...Isn't that a bit much for someone you just met?
I just got dragged into another world and turned into a pig. Today, I think I've earned the right to be rude.
Yeongnyangi fell silent for a moment.
...Fair point.
Are you an NPC?
No.
That's what all NPCs say.
...Now that you mention it, that did sound like an NPC.
I am the guardian of the River of Four Pillars.
...An NPC with lore, then.
Yeoni pressed a hoof against the flower on their head. Its petals trembled. The sensation was far too distinct.
Wow. The detail is insane.
Does it hurt?
No. It just feels weird.
Then it is real.
That is a ridiculously sloppy test.
Instead of replying, Yeongnyangi looked over the side. Yeoni followed that gaze. Only then did they properly see their surroundings.

A river. But no ordinary river. Its water was as dark blue as the night sky, starlight breaking over every ripple. Strange Chinese characters swam beneath the surface like fish: Gapja, Eulchuk, Byeongin, Jeongmyo. The sort of characters that would make you give up if they appeared on an exam.

Mist lay in the distance, with vague pillars rising beyond it. A great moon hung overhead. Its light was strangely free of cold. It was beautiful. Impossibly so. ...Which made it even more frightening.
You could wake from a dream. You could switch off a game. But this place felt like a dream with no known way to wake or turn it off.
...Where is this?
The River of Four Pillars.
Four Pillars? Like saju?
The place where the codes of human destiny flow.
Right. I understood none of that.
That is normal. Most humans understand little on their first visit.
I'm not human anymore.
A flower pig, to be precise.
I hate that word more every time I hear it.
Better than just a pig, isn't it?
...Is that meant to comfort me?
An objective analysis.
Yeoni took a deep breath. A little snort escaped. Oink, oink. An unbearably cute sound. The fact that it had come from their own mouth made them suddenly furious.
Why a pig, of all things! ...And where am I? I want to go home.
That will not be easy.
Wasn't expecting an easy answer.
Yeongnyangi walked slowly across the leaf. It glowed faintly under each step. Star-shaped markings tipped those pink paw pads. Apparently this was more than a cat that said strange things.
Yeongnyangi. Are you in charge here?
Something like that.
Then I'd like to file a complaint. Turning someone into a pig for tapping an app seems a bit excessive.
You are rather cute.
Adding that to the complaint. ...And what I tapped was an app. Code Something-or-other.
Yeongnyangi's expression stiffened a little.
That was a door.
Looked like an app.
It merely took a form humans today would readily tap. You might not open a door, but you would tap an app.
Yeoni had no comeback. It was true, which made it more annoying.
Then the water beneath the boat heaved. Splash. Yeoni instinctively ducked.
What was that?
Yeongnyangi's eyes changed. A moment ago, this had seemed like an irritated cat. Now it was different. Violet irises flared gold, and the crescent on the hat began to burn faintly.
The residue of misfortune. ...Things that leaked out of your reality.
My... reality?
Yeongnyangi pointed to black ink spreading across the river. The dark water swallowed the passing characters one by one. Their shining strokes blackened and twisted out of shape.
Your luck has been going wrong lately.

The silent alarms. The card rejected three times. The rice triangle with the wrong filling. The corrupted assignment. The canceled plans. The app that would not go away. Yeoni suddenly had nothing to say.

They had laughed it all off, but it had kept nagging at a corner of their mind. Why did everything go this wrong? Why was their timing always off? Why did even the smallest things seem to slip past them, every single time?
Does that... have something to do with this place?
Your destiny code has been damaged. The characters of your Four Pillars have scattered.
Someone messed with my saju? Why? What could possibly be worth the trouble?
To learn that, you must first reclaim your characters.
Before Yeongnyangi could finish, a black hand surged from the river. Too long to be a hand, too solid to be a shadow. Made of black water, it reached for the edge of the leaf.
Yeoni froze. Their heart dropped. Every joke they had been forcing themself to hold on to vanished. That was no piece of dream scenery. Something was coming to catch them.
Is that... coming for me?
Yes.
Why?
Because you are its target.
How can you say that so calmly!
The black hand reached over the boat. Yeoni tried to retreat, but this body still felt borrowed. Their short legs scrambled uselessly on the leaf.
Why are this body's controls so awful!
You will get used to them.
Just as the hand reached for Yeoni, Yeongnyangi vanished. Or seemed to. A golden line slashed through the air. Shhk. The hand split in two, scattering drops of ink.
Yeongnyangi landed at the leaf's edge. A small body. But there had been nothing small about that movement.
Do not call me just a cat again. I am no ordinary cat.
Yeoni considered that for a moment.
...Combat cat?
The cat's eyes narrowed.
My real name... I cannot tell you. Call me whatever you like.
Then Yeongnyangi. A mystical kitty. I'll stake one star on my naming skills.
The black hands did not disappear. More shadows rose from the river. Severed hands melted back into the water and gathered again, thicker and longer.
Yeongnyangi tapped the leaf with a paw. Tap. Clear droplets rose around its rim, forming little shields. A black hand scraped across them. Screeech.
...Worst sound ever.
They will not hold for long.
Then what do we do?
...The flower on your head is alive.
Yeoni touched it with a hoof. A petal brushed the tip. At that moment the flower glowed, very faintly. It was warm. Barely, but unmistakably.
What is it?
A trace of your Day Master. The central character that represents you.
Yeoni immediately gave up trying to understand.
Fine. For now, let's just say my flower is a battery.
It is not.
I'm putting it in terms I understand.
A mistaken understanding is dangerous.
You explain things exactly like a professor teaching a required elective.
The black hands approached again. Yeongnyangi looked across the river. Four lights emerged in the mist.
One was a sharp blue. One flickered like a warm flame. One flashed gold. The last shone as softly as an old bookshelf.
The characters of your Four Pillars are scattered across four islands. The Island of Companions. The Island of Expression. The Island of Wealth. The Library of Resources.
Yeoni looked at the four lights. Too vivid to be a dream, too chilling to be a game. Yet strangely, they seemed to be calling. Something deep inside stirred quietly.
I have to visit all of them before I can go home. Is that it?
Yes.
Hold on. I never agreed to any terms and conditions.
There is no consent procedure.
Can I get a refund halfway through?
No.
A help forum?
No.
Customer support?
...There is me, more or less.
...That makes me incredibly nervous.
Complaints are not accepted.
Worst customer service ever.
Neither are star ratings.
Then one black hand broke through the shield.
OINK—AAH!
Yeoni immediately covered their mouth.
...That was only because I got startled.
I know.

Yeongnyangi sprang up again. Golden patterns appeared on those claws. Four Pillars Starlight. With a sweep of a paw, blades of starlight fanned across the river. The black hands were severed all at once.
The lotus-leaf boat surged forward. The river parted as though opening a road. As soon as Yeongnyangi landed, a low murmur followed.
This time... I will not lose you.
Before Yeoni could ask, Yeongnyangi was already looking beyond the mist, with the eyes of someone who knew a path they had never traveled.
Our first destination is the Island of Companions.
Companions?
An island of things that resemble you.
There are more things like me?
Many. Friends, rivals, pride, jealousy—and courage.
Silently, Yeoni watched the first light in the mist. It was less beautiful than sharp, like glass. Getting close seemed likely to draw blood.
...Why does the very first island already feel wrong?
Facing yourself was never going to be comfortable.
...There you go sounding like a quote again.
Because it is true.
The lotus-leaf boat gathered speed. Behind them, black hands tore up through the river again. Ahead, the fog thickened. Beyond it, an island's silhouette slowly emerged. The Island of Companions.
Countless tiny mirror shards floated around the island. In every one, something was reflected.
